bug_semantics: A local user can make tcprewrite crash during command-line processing with a malformed range such as `--portmap -43:4443`. `tcpedit_post_args` passes the option text to `parse_portmap`, whose `ports2PORT` range branch sees the leading `-`, tokenizes `from_s` on `-`, obtains `from_begin == "43"` but no second token (`from_end == NULL`), and then calls `strtol(from_end, ...)`. The libc conversion dereferences that null pointer before any packet is rewritten, producing the reported SIGSEGV and a local denial of service.
flaw_origin: Commit 97a9237005642cf530b0b7d63c906b02460cf4dc introduced the `<port>-<port>:<port>` range feature in `src/tcpedit/portmap.c`. It first added `from_begin = strtok_r(from_s, "-", &token2)`, `from_end = strtok_r(NULL, "-", &token2)`, and unconditional `strtol` calls on both results without validating that either token exists. Later commits moved declarations and adjusted cleanup, but `git log -L` follows the same unguarded second conversion back to 97a9237005642cf530b0b7d63c906b02460cf4dc, making that feature commit the smallest causal introducer rather than a later refactor or merge.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object names human author and committer `Aaron Turner <synfinatic@gmail.com>`, has the message `first pass at improved portmap code. refs #417`, and contains no `Co-Authored-By`, `Generated-with`, bot identity, or other trailer/AI marker.
evidence: First-party report https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/971 identifies the call path `src/tcprewrite.c` -> `tcpedit_post_args` -> `parse_portmap` -> `ports2PORT` -> `strtol`, gives the reproducer `tcprewrite --portmap -43:4443 -i POC_tcprewrite_null_pointer_dereference_portmap_parsing -o /dev/null`, and records the ASan null dereference at `src/tcpedit/portmap.c:112` in revision 6fcbf0324088561d95c356fe8337f4faac275f1a.

The maintainer's first-party comment https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/issues/971#issuecomment-3199014524 says the crash is reproducible in 6fcbf03 but not in 4.5.2-beta2; the full local object for that reproduced revision is 6fcbf0324088561d95c356fe8337f4faac275f1a, a merge of the v4.5.1 release commit 0ba7d17fcb9ddedf61168f99c249b30731310d4e.

At 6fcbf0324088561d95c356fe8337f4faac275f1a, `src/tcpedit/parse_args.c:188-190` calls `parse_portmap(&tcpedit->portmap, p)` for `--portmap` and reports failure; `src/tcpedit/portmap.c:104-112` tokenizes the range and executes `long from_e = strtol(from_end, &badchar, 10)` without checking `from_end`.

`git log -L 100,112:src/tcpedit/portmap.c 6fcbf0324088561d95c356fe8337f4faac275f1a` traces the range-token extraction and unguarded `strtol(from_end, ...)` to 97a9237005642cf530b0b7d63c906b02460cf4dc (2010-03-27, `first pass at improved portmap code. refs #417`). `git log --all -S'from_end = strtok_r(NULL, "-", &token2)'` finds that feature commit and a later merge, 9d68143fe80b4a24627610fa535f27df27d58bc4; the merge is not the smallest BIC.

Direct-parent tree verification: 97a9237005642cf530b0b7d63c906b02460cf4dc has the single parent e5e6e686560627898831f679fad91755d6d1235e. `git grep -n -E 'from_end|strtok_r\(from_s, "-"|strtol\(from_end' e5e6e686560627898831f679fad91755d6d1235e -- src/tcpedit/portmap.c` returns no matches. Reading that parent tree shows only simple `<port>:<port>` parsing, with no range branch and therefore none of the vulnerable token/conversion lines; the BIC diff adds them.

The direct source fix is https://github.com/appneta/tcpreplay/commit/f6e6ee460ad9fe01e24a1579166b3f7a8c2158a7 (`Bug #94 stop on --portmap syntax error`). In `src/tcpedit/portmap.c` it changes the guard after parsing `from_begin` from `strlen(badchar) != 0` to `!from_begin || !from_end || strlen(badchar) != 0`, so the reported `-43:4443` path returns NULL before reaching `strtol(from_end, ...)`.

Release-boundary ancestry is consistent with the report. The annotated v4.5.1 tag peels to 0ba7d17fcb9ddedf61168f99c249b30731310d4e, contains BIC 97a9237005642cf530b0b7d63c906b02460cf4dc, and does not contain fix f6e6ee460ad9fe01e24a1579166b3f7a8c2158a7. The v4.5.2-beta1 tag peels to 0b0e72850228093c0864f270ea532da0f29498c6 and already contains the fix; v4.5.2-beta2 peels to a1778a25a2f8dc4de879782567abab6b923e9694 and also contains it, matching the maintainer's successful beta2 check. The final v4.5.2 tag peels to 98169912173986cc48a4ad325997dcc20c38af28 and contains the fix. Thus repository history places the first tagged patched boundary at v4.5.2-beta1, while beta2 is the first-party explicitly tested/recommended boundary.

BIC-only attribution check: `git cat-file -p 97a9237005642cf530b0b7d63c906b02460cf4dc` shows tree 50c21664dea15e4033a12bd5e82c78abb2f511e0, parent e5e6e686560627898831f679fad91755d6d1235e, author and committer Aaron Turner <synfinatic@gmail.com>, and the one-line message with no trailers. No other commit object's markers were used to attribute the BIC.
reasoning: The advisory's concrete trigger reaches argument parsing before packet processing: a leading dash selects the range branch, but there is no range-end token, so the unvalidated second `strtol` receives NULL. History follows the exact range parser back to 97a9237005642cf530b0b7d63c906b02460cf4dc. Its immediate parent e5e6e686560627898831f679fad91755d6d1235e has neither range parsing nor the vulnerable lines, while later commits only preserve, move, or reformat the already-flawed mechanism. Commit f6e6ee460ad9fe01e24a1579166b3f7a8c2158a7 directly inserts the missing-token guard that blocks the reported path, is absent from vulnerable v4.5.1, and is present in v4.5.2-beta1, v4.5.2-beta2, and v4.5.2. Finally, the BIC's own commit object has a human author/committer and no AI marker. With causal introduction, direct-parent absence, the fix, and release ancestry all proven, the appropriate closed verdict is NOT_AI.
